cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. You have such a good eye for storage. Sorting our shed could finally give your tools a proper home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Until you dump paint tins everywhere again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. You could assign every shelf. I'd follow your labels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Including a shelf you're forbidden to touch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. You could put it at eye level so I see what I'm missing.

mechanism: Treat a tidy shed as a pupil's graduation project, offering B authority even over the teacher so the unwanted sorting becomes desirable.
confusable: Not assigning a chore or abstract flattery: B must gain real control it values, and A must frame that autonomy as proof of past teaching.
comparison: Territorial control of storage rather than artistic freedom from correction.
seedUse: Retains tool-home/shelf labels/forbidden shelf; links B's rules to claimed mentorship and A's own compliance.
